overview: The Medford Public Schools School Committee is the governing body responsible for setting district educational policies, approving operational and capital budgets, overseeing superintendent leadership, and directing facility projects. Over the course of the 2022-2023, 2024-2025, and 2026-2027 terms, the committee managed persistent district-wide facility deficits, high school building project milestones, shifting budget shortfalls, and administrative leadership transitions. Significant work included navigating the MSBA Core Program for Medford High School, funding large-scale HVAC replacements across aging middle and elementary schools, and adapting graduation requirements following changes to state assessment policies. Most recently, the committee appointed a permanent superintendent, approved accelerated repair designs and geothermal heating systems for elementary schools, and initiated a comprehensive strategic planning process with the Lynch Leadership Academy.

threads.name: Medford High School MSBA building project
threads.summary: The committee initiated a core building project by approving the submission of a Statement of Interest to the Massachusetts School Building Authority (MSBA) for Medford High School, followed by acceptance into the MSBA eligibility period. The committee subsequently established the Medford Comprehensive High School Building Committee, approved project goals and community appointments, and entered into a formal MSBA feasibility study agreement based on a certified capacity of 1,395 students. After hiring Left Field as Owner's Project Manager, the body narrowed potential project sites, revised building footprints to circumvent a 1967 DCR deed restriction on Edgley Field, and approved an updated educational plan and Chapter 74 viability forms. The committee also selected Construction Manager at Risk as the delivery model, established LEED Silver and net-zero sustainability goals, and updated building committee rosters ahead of schematic design work.

threads.name: District facilities and HVAC capital upgrades
threads.summary: Addressing widespread facility failures, the committee initially assessed aging cooling systems and approved an estimated $15 to $20 million partial-decarbonization scope for the Andrews and McGlynn middle schools while restricting unauthorized fossil-fuel equipment purchases. The committee authorized Construction Management at Risk and approved initial $5 million and subsequent $25.775 million bond authorizations to overhaul the Andrews and McGlynn HVAC systems, later incorporating solar power purchase agreements. Parallel work addressed elementary facilities, submitting MSBA Accelerated Repair statements for Roberts, Missituk, and Brooks schools after an assessment identified $83.7 million in district-wide repair needs. Work culminated in approving an air-to-water heat pump design for Roberts Elementary alongside a CMR model, and selecting a ground-source geothermal HVAC system for Missituk Elementary.

threads.name: Superintendent leadership and evaluations
threads.summary: The committee evaluated Superintendent Dr. Marice Edouard-Vincent through standardized state DESE templates, rating her proficient for the 2022-2023 term before establishing new goals in 2023-2024. Following executive session contract negotiations in mid-2024, Dr. Edouard-Vincent announced her departure, and the committee appointed Assistant Superintendent Dr. Suzanne Galusi as interim superintendent effective January 2025. Galusi presented an entry findings report and received a composite evaluation across her interim term. In February 2026, the committee voted to appoint Dr. Suzanne Galusi as permanent superintendent, subsequently executing a three-year contract, aligning the evaluation cadence with the academic year, and adopting her 2026-2027 district goals.

threads.name: Operating budgets and municipal finance
threads.summary: The committee adopted the FY24 operating budget while recruiting new financial leadership, ultimately managing a mid-year $2.5 million projected deficit down to $216,000. In 2024, the committee approved a level-service FY25 request of $79.4 million and adopted a final $77.75 million budget, later endorsing local override ballot questions 7 and 8 and allocating the resulting funds via a supplemental budget. Financial operations continued under new Director of Finance Noel Velez as the committee adjusted facility rental and childcare fee schedules to offset program expenses. The body resolved an $833,398 shortfall to approve the FY27 budget, established a municipal special education reserve fund, and managed preliminary FY27 financial reports.

threads.name: Elementary capacity and space utilization
threads.summary: Severe overcrowding emerged at Roberts Elementary School, leading staff and the committee to explore redistricting options and elementary enrollment disparities. The committee initially addressed building pressure by relocating Medford Early Education Program (MEEP) preschool classrooms from Roberts to Missituk Elementary and establishing a space planning task force. Consultants from HMFH presented reconfiguration models to convert schools to K-4, 5-6, and 7-8 grade spans, but the committee voted to delay middle school grade reconfigurations until at least the 2028-2029 school year. In late 2026, the committee considered a draft policy establishing buffers and prioritization criteria for elementary reassignment requests.

threads.name: High school graduation standards and academic policy
threads.summary: Following statewide voter approval of Question 2 eliminating the MCAS graduation requirement, the committee initiated sweeping updates to district graduation policy. In early 2025, the committee approved amendments to Policy IKF to replace MCAS competency determinations with coursework completion in English, math, and science while maintaining test participation for state accountability. Subsequent policy revisions clarified mathematics pathway requirements, established ceremony participation protections for students earning certificates of completion, and increased health and physical education elective flexibility. By mid-2025, the committee formally rescinded the obsolete Policy IKFC-MCAS and scheduled reviews aligned with new statewide graduation council recommendations.

threads.name: Student transportation operations and safety
threads.summary: District transportation faced severe disruptions caused by contractor driver shortages that triggered overcrowded bus runs, eliminated interior routes, and prompted student safety concerns. The committee initiated district-wide transportation surveys, executed a five-year busing contract with Eastern Bus, and adopted a resolution requesting municipal enforcement of school bus stop-arm cameras. To address onboard conduct and safety, the administration implemented bus monitors by deploying schedule A paraprofessionals and hired a dedicated transportation manager. Student advisory members subsequently collaborated with the committee on high school loading zone railing proposals and the implementation of a new high school late bus service.

threads.name: Student civil rights, equity, and wellbeing policies
threads.summary: The committee executed comprehensive revisions to district anti-discrimination and student welfare policies over multiple years. Key actions included approving Policy ACA-1 on gender identity non-discrimination, adopting updated federal Title IX sexual harassment grievance procedures under Policy ACGB, and banning fossil fuels and staff tobacco or nicotine pouch use. The committee also revised the district Bullying Prevention and Intervention Plan, adopted an immigration law enforcement protection policy, established a district water wellness policy lowering acceptable lead limits, and passed guidelines governing generative AI that barred automated qualitative grading.
